Estimate Cohort Coefficients for Staggered Adoption

Source: R/input.R
cohort_fit.Rd

Fits an imputation or Callaway–Sant'Anna difference-in-differences estimator and constructs the joint covariance and block-bias map used by sensitivity analysis. Outcome missingness is allowed: outcomes are never imputed.

Usage

cohort_fit(
  formula = NULL,
  data,
  index,
  Y = NULL,
  D = NULL,
  estimator = "imp",
  cluster = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  ...,
  covariance = "CR1"
)

Arguments

formula

A two-variable formula such as outcome ~ treatment. Covariate terms and transformed variables are not supported by this interface.

data

A data frame of unit-period observations.

index

Character vector naming the unit and time columns, in that order.

Y, D

Outcome and treatment column names, as an alternative to formula.

estimator

One of "imp", "cs_nyt", or "cs_nt".

cluster

Cluster column name or row-aligned vector, constant within unit. Defaults to the unit identifier.

weights

Positive weights, supplied as a column name or row-aligned numeric vector. Weights must be constant within unit; the default is one. Extreme weights are rescaled by a common positive factor when required for finite arithmetic. data_info$weight_scale records that divisor; stored unit weights and cohort masses then use the rescaled units.

...

Reserved for future extensions. Unrecognized arguments cause an error.

covariance

Covariance estimator: "CR1" (default) or "CR2", case-insensitive. It follows ..., so give it by name. See Details.

Value

A cohort_fit object containing full named coefficients betahat, their joint covariance Sigma, the bias map W, normalization constraints, a cohort-period registry, sample information, and diagnostic tables. covariance_convention is "cohort_period_centered_CR1" or "cohort_period_centered_CR2". cluster_scores has one row per cluster: under CR1, Sigma is the CR1 factor times their cross-product; under CR2 the rows are the adjusted scores and Sigma is their cross-product. CR2 fits also contain cluster_shares, a data frame with one row per cluster and cohort group (cluster, cohort, units, mass, share, factor; cohort 0 is the never-treated group), and diagnostics$cr1 is NA because no CR1 factor is applied.

Details

Treatment must be binary and absorbing. Missing treatment values, including absent unit-time rows, are filled forward from the previous observed treatment status within unit. Leading unknown treatment statuses remain unknown; their outcomes are not used. At least one observed untreated period is required for every treated unit, and a never-treated group is required. An unbalanced sample uses actual observed histories for estimation; the balanced-panel bias map based on fixed cohort masses is an approximation. Estimator equivalence and the paper's coverage guarantees are not established for that approximation. A warning and diagnostic flag make this explicit.

The covariance centers outcomes within cohort-period cells (weighted cell means when weights are supplied) and sums the resulting scores within clusters. With covariance = "CR1", the default, the sum of the outer products of the cluster scores is multiplied by the CR1 factor G/(G - 1) * (n - 1)/(n - p), with G clusters, n observed usable rows, and p nonempty cohort-period cells. covariance = "CR2" is the bias-reduced covariance of Bell and McCaffrey (2002): there is no such factor, and each cluster's score is instead divided by sqrt(1 - p_c), where p_c is the cluster's share of the units of its cohort, measured by the unit weights when weights are supplied. The never-treated units form their own group. In the cohort-period cell-mean model this is the CR2 adjustment for a working model in which each unit's disturbance variance is inversely proportional to its weight. On a balanced panel, a cluster that makes up a whole cohort has a zero score under both rules, so that cohort's sampling variation is omitted. If a cluster contains units of several cohorts, the part of its score that comes from each cohort is divided by sqrt(1 - p), with p its share of that cohort; for clusters nested in cohorts this is the rule above. On unbalanced panels the CR2 adjustment, like the bias map, is an approximation: the shares are fixed by unit and do not follow the period-by-period composition of the cells, and the estimator is no longer a function of the cell means alone. There, a cluster that makes up a whole cohort still has a zero score under CR2, but if that cohort has missing outcomes, its CR1 score is generally not zero because the cluster's centered residuals no longer cancel in the estimator. The paper recommends CR2 with Conditional or C-LF inference when some cohorts contain only a few units or clusters. Few treated clusters can make either covariance unreliable even when the numerical calculation succeeds.

References

Bell, R. M. and McCaffrey, D. F. (2002). Bias reduction in standard errors for linear regression with multi-stage samples. Survey Methodology, 28(2), 169-181.

Examples

data(minimum_wage)
fit <- cohort_fit(Y ~ D, data = minimum_wage,
                  index = c("id", "year"), estimator = "cs_nt")
head(fit$betahat)
#> delta_pre_g4_s-2 delta_pre_g4_s-1  delta_pre_g4_s0 delta_pre_g6_s-4 
#>      -0.03319280      -0.01887931       0.00000000      -0.04853598 
#> delta_pre_g6_s-3 delta_pre_g6_s-2 
#>      -0.08179124      -0.03424812 
fit_cr2 <- cohort_fit(Y ~ D, data = minimum_wage, index = c("id", "year"),
                      estimator = "cs_nt", covariance = "CR2")
fit_cr2
#> Cohort difference-in-differences fit
#> Estimator: cs_nt 
#> Covariance: CR2 bias-reduced cluster-robust, 2284 clusters 
#> Cohorts: 3  | Coefficients: 21 
#>  cohort units clusters mass
#>       0  1377     1377 1377
#>       4   100      100  100
#>       6   223      223  223
#>       7   584      584  584
